_note: Named flashpoints, their gold sensitivity (0-10), and how each transmits to the price. 'typical_duration' is the honest part: most geopolitical gold rallies fade unless they change the rate path or oil supply. A flashpoint may carry 'severe_terms': phrases that are themselves the escalation and need no accompanying verb.

us_iran.name: US / Israel – Iran
us_iran.why_gold: The one flashpoint that hits gold through every channel at once. Safe-haven bid on the headline, Treasuries bid so nominal and real yields fall, and - uniquely - a credible threat to the Strait of Hormuz spikes crude, which lifts inflation expectations. Roughly a fifth of seaborne oil passes through that strait.
us_iran.counterweight: The dollar is also a haven, so risk-off bids the dollar too and cancels part of gold's gain. This is why some escalation days produce a far smaller gold move than the headlines imply.
us_iran.typical_duration: Days. Gold spikes on the exchange of fire and gives most of it back within a week unless the oil disruption is real and sustained, because only then does it reach the Fed's reaction function.
us_iran.escalation_markers: Direct state-on-state strikes rather than proxies; any interference with shipping in Hormuz; attacks on oil infrastructure; withdrawal from nuclear monitoring.

middle_east.name: Wider Middle East
middle_east.why_gold: Haven demand, mostly. Moves gold hard on the first day of a genuine escalation and then fades, because the region's conflicts rarely touch US rate expectations directly.
middle_east.counterweight: Heavily discounted by markets through repetition - a headline that would have moved gold $40 in the first month of a conflict moves it $5 in the ninth.
middle_east.typical_duration: Hours to days. The shortest-lived of the major flashpoints unless it pulls Iran in directly.
middle_east.escalation_markers: Direct Iranian involvement, Red Sea shipping disruption, or US forces taking casualties.

russia_nato.name: Russia / Ukraine / NATO
russia_nato.why_gold: Two channels: haven demand, and the structural one - sanctions on Russian reserves in 2022 taught central banks that dollar reserves can be frozen, which is a large part of why official-sector gold buying has been so persistent since.
russia_nato.counterweight: Day-to-day headlines are largely priced. The structural bid shows up in central bank demand data, not in a day's price action.
russia_nato.typical_duration: Headlines: days. The reserve-diversification effect: years, and it is arguably the single biggest reason gold has re-rated.
russia_nato.escalation_markers: Any Article 5 discussion, strikes on NATO territory, nuclear rhetoric or doctrine change, or new sanctions touching reserves or energy.

china_taiwan.name: China / Taiwan
china_taiwan.why_gold: Low frequency, very high severity. A genuine blockade or invasion scenario is the largest single tail risk in the gold market, because it would be a global supply-chain and reserve-currency event simultaneously.
china_taiwan.counterweight: Routine incursions and drills are so frequent they carry almost no information. Gold ignores them, correctly.
china_taiwan.typical_duration: Drills: nothing. A real blockade: a regime change in gold pricing, not a spike.
china_taiwan.escalation_markers: Quarantine or blockade language, live-fire exercises encircling the island, US carrier movements, or semiconductor export emergencies.

trade_tariffs.name: Trade and tariffs
trade_tariffs.why_gold: Indirect but real. Tariffs are an inflation impulse and a growth drag at once, which is the hardest combination for the Fed and therefore raises uncertainty about the rate path.
trade_tariffs.counterweight: Also dollar-positive in the short run, which works against gold. The net effect is genuinely ambiguous and often small.
trade_tariffs.typical_duration: Weeks, when it changes the inflation outlook. Announcement headlines alone rarely stick.
trade_tariffs.escalation_markers: Rates above expectations, retaliation, or extension to critical minerals and energy.

fed_independence.name: Fed independence and US fiscal stress
fed_independence.why_gold: The most underrated gold driver on this list. Gold is a hedge against monetary credibility, so anything that threatens the central bank's independence or the Treasury's standing goes to the heart of why the asset is owned at all.
fed_independence.counterweight: Nothing meaningful - this is one of the few themes where the haven bid and the rates channel push the same way.
fed_independence.typical_duration: Long. Credibility is repriced slowly and recovers slowly; these episodes have lasting effects on the gold bid rather than one-day spikes.
fed_independence.escalation_markers: Explicit attempts to remove or pressure Fed officials, ratings actions, a failed or badly-covered auction, or a shutdown running long enough to delay official data.

korea.name: Korean peninsula
korea.why_gold: Classic haven headline risk, heavily desensitised by decades of repetition.
korea.counterweight: Markets have learned to fade it almost entirely.
korea.typical_duration: Hours, unless a test is genuinely novel in capability.
korea.escalation_markers: A nuclear test, an ICBM over Japan, or any exchange of fire across the DMZ.
